Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

there was a time when phrase

also there was a time, time was when, once there was a time

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.2.2: fuit quoddam tempus cum in agrīs hominēs bēstiārum mōre vagābantur (Lewis & Short s.v. cum)
Varr. RR 3.1: fuit tempus cum rūra colerent hominēs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 89, 395

fuit (quoddam) tempus cum …

cum with the indicative, or the subjunctive; tempus may be left out: fuit cum …

Latin says it as English does, with cum for “when”.

Examples

  • fuit quoddam tempus cum in agrīs hominēs bēstiārum mōre vagābantur

    there was a time when men wandered the fields like wild beastsCic. Inv. 1.2.2 (Lewis & Short s.v. cum)

See also once upon a time, long ago, used to.

SourcesLewis & Short: cum · Lewis & Short: tempus

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
